This bill is part of a package that would create a new Aviation Consumer Protection Framework to improve the flying experience for passengers.

The framework would let the minister set minimum standards for airline and airport services, and would set up a new regulator called the Aviation Consumer Protection Authority to oversee compliance and enforce those standards.

An independent Aviation Consumer Ombuds Scheme would handle aviation-specific complaints, and the bill would also establish an Aircraft Noise Ombudsperson within the department to review noise complaint handling by Airservices Australia and the Department of Defence.
Establishes the Aviation Consumer Protection Framework.
Enables the minister to issue an Aviation Consumer Protections Charter with minimum service standards.
Creates the Aviation Consumer Protection Authority for monitoring, compliance and enforcement.
Authorises an external dispute resolution scheme, the Aviation Consumer Ombuds Scheme, overseen by the Aviation Consumer Ombudsperson.
Establishes the Aircraft Noise Ombudsperson to review how Airservices Australia and the Department of Defence handle noise complaints.
Aviation consumers, airlines, airport operators, Airservices Australia, and the Department of Defence.
